lessons.title: Reading an academic argument
lessons.feedback: Your argument structure is improving. Next, make the evidence-to-claim connection more explicit.

lesson_materials.title: Academic Argument Guide
lesson_materials.content: A claim tells the reader what you think. Evidence gives an observation or example. Commentary explains why the evidence supports the claim. Use a short because bridge to make the relationship explicit.

lesson_materials.title: Evidence & Commentary
lesson_materials.content: Evidence: students respond to competing interpretations in a seminar. Explanation: defending assumptions makes reasoning clearer. Claim: seminar discussion improves argument quality.

observations.text: Ivy states a claim clearly. Next lesson: explain how a source supports it.

payload.question: How do I explain the link between my evidence and my main claim?
payload.answer: Use a short because bridge: give the evidence, explain what it shows, and connect that explanation to your main claim.

payload.question: May I cite an unpublished seminar recording?
payload.answer: The teaching corpus does not establish the recording’s citation and permission rules. Emily will review this question.
